id: title:jurajmajerik:log pause and resume in experiment history

review.posthog_relevance: Adds audit trail and human-readable status indicators for experiment lifecycle events (pause/resume) in the PostHog experimentation module, supporting operational visibility and debugging.
review.reason: The change implements three complementary hunks: P1.F3.H1 adds backend activity logging, P1.F2.H1 adds frontend rendering, and P1.F1.H1 adds the activity type definitions. This establishes a complete, bounded implementation for recording and displaying experiment pause/resume events. This is a substantive, bounded capability improvement rather than a narrow maintenance change.
review.uncertainty: The tier is assigned based on the presence of implementation and logging, not on verified operational benefit or incident avoidance. The actual impact on user workflow or system reliability is not independently verified.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs detected. No missing context. No untrusted instructions. No score assigned yet.

observations.behavior: Adds two new activity types, 'paused' and 'resumed', to the experiment activity description and backend logging.
observations.posthog_connection: Adds human-readable descriptions for experiment pause and resume events in the frontend activity log, and records backend activity entries for these events.

observations.behavior: Adds implementation for the 'paused' and 'resumed' activity types in the activity describer, including user and experiment name, and links to the experiment.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides the frontend rendering and description for pause and resume events, including the user who performed the action and the experiment name.

observations.behavior: Adds backend logging for the pause and resume activities, including the user, organization, team, and experiment details.
observations.posthog_connection: Records the pause and resume events in the backend activity log, allowing users to see who performed the action and when, and linking to the experiment.
